transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I know a few people in my department have quietly agreed to block my grants and promotions, and I can’t shake that belief no matter how much my wife or colleagues argue with me. It is incredibly frustrating because I see the signs of it constantly, even if everyone else tells me I'm just overthinking it.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to enjoy your usual hobbies, or have you found it difficult to keep up with your daily hygiene or social interactions over the past six months?

My daily hygiene, routine, and teaching duties are completely fine, and I still try to keep up with my hobbies like hiking and brewing. However, I've been skipping department socials and avoiding certain colleagues because of my suspicions, which has really strained my relationships at work. Spending my evenings tracking committee rosters instead of relaxing has also put a lot of tension on my marriage.
Have you ever experienced hearing voices that others cannot hear, or have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcasted or controlled by an outside force?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never heard voices that aren't there, and I certainly don't feel like my thoughts are being controlled or broadcasted by anyone else.
How long have you held the belief that your colleagues are working against you, and do you feel that this specific concern is the only area of your life where your perspective differs from others?

This has been going on for about a year now, starting right after I missed out on a major grant and a younger colleague got a faculty job. Yes, this is the only area where my perspective differs, as I still handle my daily teaching duties and home life normally. The only real friction is when I avoid certain colleagues or turn down projects because I suspect they are part of the plot, which has strained my relationships at work and at home.
Have you ever used any substances, or have you been diagnosed with any physical health conditions that your doctor suggested might be affecting your mood or thinking?

No, I do not use any substances, and I have never been diagnosed with any physical health conditions that could affect my mood or thinking. Aside from the stress of this situation, my physical health is perfectly fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent, non-bizarre delusional belief (persecutory in nature) regarding colleagues sabotaging his career, lasting for one year. He lacks other symptoms of schizophrenia (hallucinations, thought broadcasting, disorganized speech) and maintains overall functioning in daily life and professional duties, except for specific avoidant behaviors related to the delusion.
